title: A trailer for a game I've made in 1.5 weeks | Wizards Go Farming
author: MomicaX
selftext:
I've spent the past week and a half building this game! All coding, sprite gen, visuals, and trailer creation was made with Claude. I am a developer who has done small game projects before and I've been really trying to see how polished/good a game can look with good direction/game design. I think it will only get better. I wanted to show it off because I'm almost ready to release a demo! Let me know if you have any questions or what you think!

Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5350880/Wizards\_Go\_Farming/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=social&utm\_campaign=aigamedev](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5350880/Wizards_Go_Farming/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aigamedev)

comments.author: kiapakaru
comments.body: Looks good! What engine did you use? And what is your workflow creating the visuals?

replies.author: MomicaX
replies.body: Thanks! I used Unity as I've used it in the past and they released a Unity CLI which allows Claude to do a lot of the things you'd normally have to do in the Unity App. My workflow for creating visuals involved setting strict requirements in the beginning. I set a specific color palette, pixel density, target dimension, and gave constantly iterated. I was almost never satisfied with the first generation, so I had to give it very specific feedback on what I liked/didn't like. I redid a lot of the visuals in huge iterations a few times. Figuring out what didn't look right and asking it to provide potential solutions/ visuals for me to pick from helped a lot. I didn't try to get too complicated with external tools so all of the sprites/animations/UI was made directly in a Claude chat!

comments.author: andrewlewi
comments.body: This is insane for one and a half weeks!!! I cant wait to see what people will cook up in the future with more time and better models 👀

replies.author: MomicaX
replies.body: Ty! I've been using codex/claude for a few months in work and on the side and it's crazy how much the models are improving alongside my ability to use them. Even if you aren't making anything shippable, I think the best thing you can do right now is just play around with them to see what's possible! Also happy cake day!
